notes:
Inbound self-serve signup -> early discovery. Team: 3 backend engs, 2 frontend, product lead. Wants hosted API (low ops) + streaming for real-time agent UI. Primary pain: structured JSON mode + function/tool-calling reliability.

Call notes (03/03): 'When we enable JSON mode the UI randomy gets partial objects — sometimes last chunk is truncated and parse fails.' Frontend dev paraphrase: 'We rely on complete objects per turn to call tools; streaming breaks that expectation.'

Observed symptoms: truncated final token on ~20% of streams (dev repro), occasional mismatch where function name returned doesn't match schema registered client-side, arguments show flattened strings instead of expected typed fields (e.g., {"order_id":"123"} vs {"order_id":123}). They use a wrapper that validates schema then calls a webhook tool. Failures cause agent to fallback to non-actionable text.

Customer asked about: recommended backoff/retry semantics for streaming JSON, tooling to validate function schema on model response before calling, sample robust client patterns (buffer until close-delimiter + streaming-aware incremental-parse), and whether Redwood hosted API has an option to force non-streamed finalization or emit JSON-safe chunks.

Quoted from product lead: 'We want a low-friction fix — ideally something in the SDK or config flags so our UI can rely on deterministic tool calls.'
